flags.observation: No style file among critic inputs; genre family, 100-130 BPM and danceability cannot be verified. Lyric format matches the golden.
Thesis "Alice gets a guilty verdict before the trial" misattributes: the cards convict the Knave; Alice is never sentenced in the card source.
Single onboarding beat: the stand-up joke lands, but nobody says who speaks or what happens here; intro and outro carry no expert dog whistle.
"a poem about tarts" is unsupported; the card source only says the evidence is a poem that makes no sense.
Opener "Alice chases a summons to:" reads ungrammatically against the card name and has no link to the rabbit's lateness.
Bare rule labels tacked on as tags: "Hookah haze" here, "Gaslight" in beat 5, "Narcolepsy" in beat 8.
"marmalade jar fall" breaks grammar at line end; four nouns plus a stray verb are hard to say in one breath.
Openers mostly navigate places ("Into the hole:", "One sip:"); few give a card a want, wound or grudge.
"time loop, repeat the last sentence" recites the power as a game instruction, not as an aside or inversion.
Opener "the verdict returns" lets an abstraction act like a person.
"After croquet" is temporal sequencing, an and-then link; same pattern in beat 15 "Past the clocks, she enters".
"Giant can intimidate the King" and "the Giant grows" use the game state Giant; beat 23 uses "Micro" the same way.
"Micro hides inside the other bottle": the card hides inside other cards; the second bottle is a new image.
"heads grow, tails shrink, edge a neck like a serpent" recites the coin-flip mechanic; unparseable for a listener without the rule.
Slate-Pencil line recites the annoyance rule; "SCREECH, screech" doubles the sound word.
Opener "The soldiers hide their mistake with:" pre-explains the card goal "conceal a mistake", breaking closure.
Opener "She tries the riddle before:" dangles; the tarts card neither follows from nor twists the riddle.
Outro callback works but restates the intro parking joke; the power statement in beat 33 stays inside the deck plot.
